Bang & Olufsen Says Turnaround Strategy Is Gaining Traction
By Dominic Chopping
Bang & Olufsen said its strategic reset is moving the business forward as it reported higher sales in its fiscal first quarter.

The Danish consumer-electronics company is working through a turnaround plan that targets growth through enhancing customer experience and brand awareness while expanding in key growth markets and investing in new products.
Last month a new executive team was appointed, with Gianfilippo Testa, a luxury-industry veteran who most recently was head of Alexander McQueen, taking over as chief executive.

Pandora's Jesper Hessel will assume the newly created role of chief commercial officer and deputy CEO, while the company also said Chief Financial Officer Nikolaj Wendelboe would add the role of chief operating officer to his current duties.
The company said Wednesday that like-for-like customer sales grew 7% in the period, driven by Europe, Middle East and Africa, and Asia Pacific, while the gross margin hit a record high of 59.4%.
Revenue rose to 530 million Danish kroner ($80.4 million) from 517 million kroner, confirming preliminary results pre-released Tuesday.

"The results show that the strategy is moving the business in the right direction," said CEO Testa. "However, certain areas of the business still need increased attention and more consistent execution."
The results were due to be released next week but the company brought the announcement forward after realizing some figures had been inadvertently disclosed to media.
